look_here_first: DALLISGRASS: on ONE complete seedhead count about 3–7(11) laterally spreading one-sided racemes. Its mature spikelets are generally 3–4 mm, broadly ovate and conspicuously LONG-SILKY-HAIRED at the upper-glume margins. Compare with vaseygrass: often 10–20 racemes and smaller 2–3 mm spikelets; these counts overlap. Existing Joey photos show the true racemes and leaf collar area, NOT measured ligules or the decisive silky margins.

crew_field_steps: See the mature inflorescence as a whole: several slender arching racemes attached at different heights on a central flowering axis.
At the leaf blade/sheathed stem junction, the existing Joey photograph visibly shows a blade-base and pale collar hair area, but no independently measured membranous ligule.
For species confirmation, magnify a full mature flattened spikelet, its margin hairs and a ruler; counts/height alone overlap P. urvillei.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Entire flowering culm with lower branches and count on ONE head.
Single complete branch at scale showing rows of spikelets and attachment.
Several mature spikelets in side/face view under 10–20×, ruler beside 3–4 mm units and long edge hairs.
Leaf collar membrane and sheath mouth (correct part clearly exposed); compare vaseygrass.
Rooted tuft size and basal sheaths.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Paspalum: what to inspect
steps: Photograph entire panicle with all raceme attachment points on SAME culm; follow one raceme from its base. On 5 detached mature 3–4 mm spikelets record true silky marginal hairs and upper-glume outline. Leaf collar photo is a site-reference only.
First show the WHOLE head, then ONE one-sided raceme and attached spikelets. Never treat a photograph of one branch as total raceme count.
Obtain a real intact mature spikelet and measure it with 1-mm reference; use margin hair pattern and glumes to separate close Paspalum taxa.
Photograph blade/sheath joint and same-plant rootstock; knotgrass needs actually rooted horizontal stolons, not merely a low mat.
If plant photo is source-labelled only, keep identity tentative and leave existing county-native fields unchanged.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Dallisgrass usually 3–7 racemes with larger silky-margined spikelets, while vaseygrass commonly 10–20 racemes and smaller roughly 2–3 mm spikelets; counts overlap. Florida paspalum generally has fewer long branches and broad large oval spikelets. Bahia grass generally has two terminal racemes and lacks the distinct long marginal silky fringe characteristic of dallisgrass.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Gross photo structures are references, NOT expert confirmation. Even new licensed images are PROVISIONAL — USER PHOTO REVIEW PENDING and not proof of Hays County presence.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.details: On ONE complete flowering culm, follow each branch from its attachment on the main axis. Dallisgrass is a coarse perennial with spreading to drooping racemes and paired overlapping spikelets in rows on the underside. Existing panel 0 teaches the branching habit but overlapping plants prevent a reliable total count. Branch count alone does NOT separate vaseygrass.
field_id_short_tiles.status: VISIBLE HEAD; WHOLE SAME-PLANT PANICLE GAP

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · FOLLOW THE ROOTED TUFT
field_id_short_tiles.short: Perennial clump with short rhizomes, not long stolons
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published Williamson County plants have a fibrous-rooted perennial tuft and short rhizomes with nodal roots; basal sheaths can be hairy. A complete same-plant root-to-head photograph with centimeter scale is missing. Do not infer underground rhizomes from the existing detached flowering-head panels.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED GROWTH FORM; ROOTED CROWN PHOTO GAP

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Membranous ligule 2–5.5 mm in local treatment
field_id_short_tiles.details: Pull back the leaf blade at its INNER junction with the sheath. The Williamson County treatment describes a translucent membranous ligule 2–5.5 mm, with separate hairs on the upper collar; broader GrassBase accounts allow 2–8 mm. Panels 1–2 show an external junction and pale hairs, NOT a measured ligule. Never measure collar hairs as the membrane.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE MATURE SPIKELETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Typically 3–4 mm; paired and broadly ovate
field_id_short_tiles.details: Find five ripe spikelets on a single one-sided raceme, then photograph their flat and convex faces beside a physical 1-mm ruler at 10–20×. Williamson County describes the upper glume at 3.5–3.7 × 2.2–2.4 mm, while wider GrassBase spikelet ranges are 2.7–3.9 mm. Existing gallery panels 4–5 are source-identified photographs, not verified millimeter measurements.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · FIND THE SILKY UPPER GLUME
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower glume absent; upper glume silky-edged; awnless
field_id_short_tiles.details: Dissect one ripe two-flowered spikelet. The lower glume is absent; the upper glume is spikelet-length, 5–7-veined in the Williamson County treatment (broader treatments 3–9), and fringed with long silky hairs. The lower sterile lemma is near glume-length; the hard, glossy upper fertile lemma is about 2.2 mm locally (2–3.2 mm in broader accounts). There is NO long true awn: marginal glume hairs are not awns. No existing panel certifies all bract identities.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — DISSECTED GLUME/LEMMA WITH HAIR ORIGIN

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · SEPARATE VASEYGRASS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Dallisgrass usually fewer racemes and larger silky spikelets
field_id_short_tiles.details: Paspalum urvillei commonly has more slender racemes (often 10–20) and smaller ripe spikelets (~2–3 mm), but head counts and spikelet sizes can overlap. Panel 3 is explicitly a DIFFERENT-SPECIES vaseygrass reference, not a Dallisgrass image. Compare equally mature, ruler-scaled spikelets, upper-glume hair placement, and a whole head from each species; avoid using wet habitat or clump size alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD LOOK-ALIKE CUE; MATCHED DIAGNOSTIC MACROS MISSING
